label: Interfaces & screens
intent: Software that looks real. Screen contents must be plausible, aligned and correctly spelled.

recipes.when: You need one screen that looks like a shipping product, not a wireframe.
recipes.text:
Create a {ratio} mockup of the {subject} screen of a real-looking mobile app.
SCREEN CONTENT — invent a plausible product and populate the screen with real interface copy: a real title, real navigation labels, real list items with real names, realistic numbers and dates. Every string must be a correctly spelled word or phrase that belongs on that screen. No placeholder text, no lorem ipsum, no keyboard mash.
LAYOUT — strict alignment: one consistent grid, one consistent left margin, consistent spacing between elements, a clear hierarchy of title, body and metadata. Tap targets look genuinely tappable.
TYPE — {type}, a clear three-level hierarchy.
PRESENTATION — the screen shown flat and head-on, scaled to fill the frame, {composition}, on {background}. Optionally one soft device shadow.
COLOUR — {grading}. LIGHTING — {lighting}.

image.accepts: a screenshot or an existing UI
image.skeleton:
Use the supplied screenshot as the exact structural reference. Keep its layout, navigation and content hierarchy recognisable.

Re-render it as a polished {ratio} {subject} screen mockup with real interface copy: correct titles, labels, list items and realistic figures, all properly spelled. Strict alignment on one grid with consistent spacing and a clear type hierarchy. {type}, {grading}. Present it flat and head-on, {composition}, on {background}. Improve the visual craft without changing what the screen does.

negatives: no more than one device shadow
recipes.example: Create a 9:16 mockup of the home screen of a real-looking mobile app for tracking houseplants. SCREEN CONTENT — title "My Plants", four list rows each with a real plant name and a real last-watered date, a bottom navigation bar labelled Today, Plants, Schedule and Me, and a small status line reading "3 need water today". Every string correctly spelled. LAYOUT — strict single-column grid, consistent left margin, consistent spacing, clear hierarchy between plant name and metadata. TYPE — bold geometric sans in three sizes. PRESENTATION — flat and head-on, centred hero, on a dark textured background with one soft device shadow. COLOUR — neutral and true.

recipes.goal: A designed page that presents work as a case study.
recipes.when: Portfolio piece, marketing page, design-process writeup. Image plus structure plus a little story.
recipes.text:
Create a {ratio} page presenting {subject} as a design case study.
LAYOUT — a real editorial page on a strict grid: a wide title block at the top, one large hero image, then two columns of shorter supporting content below it.
TITLE — the exact text "{text}" as the page headline, set in {type} at the largest size on the page.
SUPPORTING CONTENT — real sentences, correctly spelled, describing the problem, the approach and the outcome. Two short paragraphs, no filler, no repeated words.
STRUCTURE — a clear three-level type hierarchy, consistent baseline grid, generous margins, and one accent colour used to mark section labels only.
BACKGROUND — {background}. COLOUR — {grading}.
RENDER — a clean, flat designed page. No device frame, no perspective, no gloss.
negatives: no more than three type sizes
recipes.example: Create a 3:4 page presenting a redesign of a bicycle repair booking flow as a design case study. LAYOUT — wide title block at the top, one large hero image of the new booking screen, then two columns of supporting text below. TITLE — the exact text "BOOKING, REBUILT" as the headline in bold geometric sans, the largest element on the page. SUPPORTING CONTENT — two short real paragraphs: one on why the old flow lost people at the date step, one on what changed and the measured result. STRUCTURE — three type sizes, consistent baseline grid, generous margins, one accent colour marking the two section labels. BACKGROUND — seamless white. COLOUR — neutral and true. RENDER — flat designed page, no device frame or perspective.

recipes.goal: A screen element seen in the world — camera view, AR overlay, heads-up display.
recipes.when: You need the product to feel embedded in reality rather than shown on a device.
recipes.text:
Create a {ratio} first-person point-of-view photograph of {subject}.
CAMERA — a real handheld viewpoint: slight tilt, natural framing, mild motion blur at the edges. It should feel photographed, not rendered.
OVERLAY — a minimal heads-up interface floating in the view: two or three small labelled markers, thin leader lines, one short status line, all in {type}. The overlay is perfectly crisp while the photographed world behind it is soft. Every label must be a real, correctly spelled word.
COMPOSITION — {composition}. The overlay must never obscure the thing it is annotating.
LIGHTING — {lighting}. COLOUR — {grading}. MOOD — {mood}.
negatives: no more than four interface elements
recipes.example: Create a 9:16 first-person point-of-view photograph of a supermarket shelf being scanned while shopping. CAMERA — handheld, slightly tilted, the shelf filling the frame at a natural arm's length, mild blur at the edges. OVERLAY — a thin rectangle around one cereal box, a small label above it reading "Matches your list", a second label reading "2 for 5.00", and one status line at the top reading "List: 6 of 9". Overlay crisp, world soft. COMPOSITION — overhead, the overlay never covering the product it marks. LIGHTING — natural window light from the aisle end. COLOUR — neutral and true. MOOD — calm.
